title: Legislative districts of Occidental Mindoro
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Occidental Mindoro''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Occidental Mindoro]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Occidental Mindoro's at-large congressional district|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Mindoro}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Occidental Mindoro were represented under the [[Mindoro's at-large congressional district|lone district]] of the undivided [[Mindoro (province)|Mindoro Province]] from 1898 to 1951. The enactment of Republic Act No. 505 on June 13, 1950 split the old Mindoro Province into [[Occidental Mindoro]] and [[Oriental Mindoro]], and provided each of them separate representation in Congress.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=505|title=An Act to Create the Provinces of Oriental Mindoro and Occidental Mindoro|date=June 13, 1950|accessdate=November 28, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=http://www.thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-505.php}} Pursuant to Section 6 of R.A. 505, the incumbent representative of Mindoro continued to serve the entire province until Occidental Mindoro's [[Legislative district of Oriental Mindoro#Lone District|separate representative]] was elected in a [[List of special elections to the Philippine Congress#House of Representatives|special election]] held on the same day as the [[1951 Philippine Senate election|1951 senatorial elections]]. Occidental Mindoro was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province constituted a [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone congressional district]],{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|accessdate=November 19, 2017}} and elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. Beginning in 2019, the districts used in appropriation of members is coextensive with the legislative districts of Occidental Mindoro. Prior to 2019 while the province was just one congressional district, the Commission on Elections divided the province into two [[Occidental Mindoro Provincial Board|provincial board]] districts. ==Current districts== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives of [[Occidental Mindoro]] |- !District ! colspan="3" | Current Representative !Party !Population (2020) !Area |- ![[Occidental Mindoro's at-large congressional district|Lone]] | style="background:{{party color| Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}};" | |[[File:Rep.
